name: catalog_tuple_degeneracy

phase_0.boundary_condition: The IG catalog kernel with its generated subset, deduplication logic, and runtime audit surface — a closed system where tuple degeneracy is measured, classified, and repaired at a single site.

VINIT.justification: The void state before any catalog entries exist — no tuples assigned, no collisions detected, no repair criterion applied.

TANCH.justification: The closed containment of the catalog system: generated subset, static catalog, deduplication merge, and redteam audit surface — nothing enters or leaves without passing through the repair criterion.

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism that assigns 12-primitive tuples to catalog entries, propagating structure from the grammar into the catalog.

AREV.justification: Reverse descent that traces a collision back to its origin — whether a name duplicate, cross-domain tier mismatch, or tuple→word collapse — exposing the causal path for repair.

CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining that composes individual tuple assignments into the complete catalog structure, and composes collision classes into the repair decision.

IMSCRIB.justification: The repair criterion imscribes itself: it is a tuple collision classifier that must also classify its own tuple without degeneracy.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits each collision class into two arms: coherent (grammar identifying a kind) and incoherent (defect requiring repair).

FFUSE.justification: Rejoins the coherence arms into a single graded verdict — conflicting arms fuse to B (both kind-identifying and defect held), which IS the repair criterion.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative arm: collision class where all members agree on domain AND tier — the grammar correctly identifies a kind (98.3% of classes).

EVALF.justification: Negative arm: collision class with domain/tier disagreement — a defect (1.7% of classes), e.g., IUG class spanning General/Language/Mathematics at tiers 0/4.

ENGAGR.justification: Holds both coherent and incoherent simultaneously without resolution — the criterion does not discard collisions as noise but grades them: some ARE the grammar, some are defects, both are real.

IFIX.justification: Permanent, append-only record of the single chosen repair site and its graded classification — cannot be undone by catalog regeneration.

split_outputs: coherent arm: all members agree on domain AND tier
incoherent arm: members disagree on domain OR tier
phase_2.fuse_result: graded classification: coherent classes = grammar identifying a kind; incoherent classes = defects; the fusion holds both as B (paradice) — this IS the repair criterion
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Catalog before initialization: no entries, no tuples, no collisions, no criterion.
phase_3.true_description: Coherent collision class confirmed as grammar identifying a kind; repair site confirmed as the single correct location.
phase_3.false_description: Incoherent collision class confirmed as defect; repair site candidate rejected.
phase_3.both_description: Graded criterion holding coherent and incoherent simultaneously (paradice); conflicting repair-site candidates fused to a single B-state resolution.

steps.domain_action: catalog genesis — void state before any entries exist
fork into tuple assignment completeness check
forward morphism — assign 12-primitive tuples to all catalog entries from grammar
compose individual assignments into complete catalog structure
affirmative — all entries have tuples assigned (assignment complete)
reverse descent — check for entries missing tuples or with malformed tuples
negative — entries without valid tuples (assignment defect)
rejoin — assignment phase complete (mixed → B if defects exist)
fork into collision detection
forward — detect all tuple collisions (shared tuples across entries)
compose collisions into collision classes (842 classes covering 3242 entries)
fork into coherence evaluation (nested inner fork)
affirmative — coherent class: all members agree on domain AND tier (grammar identifying a kind)
paradice — hold coherent classification without resolving away
reverse — evaluate incoherence: cross-domain, cross-tier, duplicate names within class
negative — incoherent class: domain/tier disagreement (defect)
paradice — hold incoherent classification without resolving away
rejoin inner fork — coherence evaluated, conflicting arms fuse to B (graded: both kind and defect real)
paradice — graded criterion: the collision IS the grammar identifying a kind AND a defect simultaneously, held without collapse
rejoin outer fork — all collisions classified by graded criterion
fork into repair site selection (four candidates)
affirmative — candidate 1: generated file (catalog_ask_subset.rs)
paradice — hold candidate 2: generator that emits the file
paradice — hold candidate 3: catalog_init() deduplication step
reverse — evaluate candidate 4: runtime validation (redteam audit / shadow)
negative — candidate 4 alone insufficient (bare-metal no_std, no filesystem)
paradice — hold candidate 2 on F-arm
paradice — hold candidate 3 on F-arm
rejoin — single repair site selected: conflicting arms fuse to B (the generator site, where tuple assignment originates)
self-reference — repair criterion imscribes itself: it classifies its own tuple without degeneracy
permanent fixation — repair decision and site recorded in ROM, append-only, survives catalog regeneration
terminal anchor — closed boundary: kernel + generated subset + criterion + fixation = complete system

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The tuple assignment logic that maps 12 primitives to catalog entries — translates grammar intentions into tuple operations.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Collision class propagation: coherent classes flow as kind-identifiers; incoherent classes flow as defect reports to the repair site.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Static catalog (hand-written ladder) merged with generated subset (56k lines) — deduplication by name only, tuple collisions preserved in memory.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Catalog initialization sequence: static load → generated merge → deduplication → collision detection → criterion application → fixation.
phase_5.alfs_store: The grounded tuple ⟨ at crystal address 6,734,591 — the canonical bootstrap store for this domain.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One tuple assignment per entry; one collision classification per shared tuple; one repair-site fusion per catalog cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Catalog with unclassified collisions (29.7% entries in collision classes, 1.7% incoherent), no graded criterion, no fixed repair site.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Catalog with every collision graded (coherent = kind, incoherent = defect, both held), single repair site fixed at generator, criterion self-imscribed and fixated.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the cycle converts structural ambiguity (degeneracy) into graded information (criterion) without loss; fixation preserves the gain across regenerations.

banked_count_check.verdict: 9 unit(s) survived a clear by being banked in a frame (3 live clear(s)); 10 further unit(s) flattened by a fold between sibling regions and not restored
banked_count_check.surplus_note: a split between two deposits of the same value puts them in sibling regions; the fold keeps the larger rather than the sum. Put them in one region to keep both.
